target.title: fix: block mixed-case cron shell jobs from agent tool [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agent-created cron jobs could bypass the agent cron tool's shell-execution restriction when cron kind values used alternate casing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent cron tool now applies the same case-insensitive kind interpretation used by cron normalization when enforcing its shell-execution deny rule. CLI and Gateway cron command support are unchanged; this only tightens the agent-tool boundary before dispatching `cron.add` or `cron.update`.

## User Impact

Agent tool calls can no longer create or edit command-backed cron jobs through mixed-case payload or schedule kinds. Normal agent-turn and system-event cron jobs continue to work through the existing cron tool flow.

## Evidence

AI-assisted.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 144 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Remote Testbox/AWS Crabbox proof was unavailable in this environment before source sync: installed Crabbox is 0.20.0 for Testbox, and the AWS broker is not logged in on this host.


Additional current-head behavior proof:

- `node --import tsx --eval '<cron tool denied-path harness>'` exercised `createCronTool().execute(...)` without a mocked Gateway for mixed-case shell-backed add/update inputs. Output:

```text
mixed-case command payload add: DENIED_BEFORE_GATEWAY: cron command payloads cannot be created or edited through the agent cron tool; use the CLI or Gateway API.
mixed-case on-exit schedule add: DENIED_BEFORE_GATEWAY: cron on-exit schedules cannot be created or edited through the agent cron tool; use the CLI or Gateway API.
mixed-case command payload update: DENIED_BEFORE_GATEWAY: cron command payloads cannot be created or edited through the agent cron tool; use the CLI or Gateway API.
mixed-case on-exit schedule update: DENIED_BEFORE_GATEWAY: cron on-exit schedules cannot be created or edited through the agent cron tool; use the CLI or Gateway API.
```

This proves the denied inputs fail inside the real cron tool executor before a Gateway dispatch is needed. The positive control remains the focused cron-tool suite above, which includes allowed agent-turn cron add/update paths.
